title: The object of maps from a finite simplicial set into a simplicial semi-representable object exists
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme, let $K$ be a simplicial object of the category $\mathrm{SR}(X)$ of semi-representable objects over $X$ [def-weil-pbc-semi-representable-object], and let $S$ be a simplicial set [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set] such that $S_n$ is finite and nonempty for every $n\geq0$ and $S$ has finitely many nondegenerate simplices. Then there are an object $H$ of $\mathrm{SR}(X)$ and morphisms $u_s:H\to K_n$ ($n\geq0$, $s\in S_n$) with $K(\varphi)\circ u_s=u_{S(\varphi)(s)}$ for every $\varphi:[m]\to[n]$ and $s\in S_n$, such that for every object $W$ of $\mathrm{SR}(X)$ and every family of morphisms $f_s:W\to K_n$ ($n\geq0$, $s\in S_n$) with $K(\varphi)\circ f_s=f_{S(\varphi)(s)}$ for all $\varphi$ and $s$, there is a unique morphism $g:W\to H$ with $f_s=u_s\circ g$ for all $s$.
